title: NeuPIMs: NPU-PIM Heterogeneous Acceleration for Batched LLM Inferencing
technique: NPU+PIM heterogeneous accelerator with dual row buffers and sub-batch interleaving to overlap GEMM (NPU) and GEMV (PIM)

optimized_metrics.evidence: We architect NeuPIMs such that it effectively balances the utilization of memory bandwidth and computational resources of the system to improve the overall inference throughput.
architect NeuPIMs such that it effectively balances the utilization of memory bandwidth and computational resources of the system to improve the overall inference throughput

headline_claim.text: compared to GPU-only, NPU-only, and a naive NPU+PIM integrated acceleration approaches, NeuPIMs achieves 3x, 2.4x and 1.6x throughput improvement, respectively.

reported_metrics.where: Table 4 NPU/PIM compute and memory bandwidth utilization

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we simulate the inference serving for a fixed amount of time, randomly picking sequence lengths from the datasets ... We sample 10 different batches and use them to measure the throughputs of different hyperparameter combinations.
metric_definitions.notes: Throughput unit is 1k tokens/s (Fig 14); input vs output token counting is never defined; simulated batches, not request arrivals.

load_regime: fixed batch sizes (64-512) of sampled sequence lengths; throughput of steady-state batches
tradeoff_acknowledged: none; says batching improves utilization 'while not sacrificing the latency requirement' without measuring latency
hardware: NPU+PIM (cycle-accurate simulator extension), baselines A100 40GB and TPU-like NPU
